title: Classic Mac Games
description: Games, toys, screensavers and demos for the original black-and-white Macintosh: an 8 MHz 68000, a 1-bit screen and System 6. Written in C and built on a modern Mac.

modules.name: growcity
modules.label: GrowCity, a tiny isometric city that grows on its own

modules.html:
Designing for 1 bit and 8 MHz

These run on a stock Mac Plus, SE or Classic with 1 to 4 MB of RAM, or in an emulator. Every frame has to read in pure black and white, and every effect has to fit a 68000 with no floating-point unit. I measure real 8 MHz frame rates with a cycle-accurate emulator, so what you see is what the original hardware does.

Games

  • One Foe, an original single-boss bullet-hell duel with four attack phases.
  • Celeste Classic, a port of the PICO-8 original.
  • Just One Boss, a port of the PICO-8 one-boss bullet dodger, made with its creator's permission.
  • GrowCity, a tiny city-growing toy.

Toys and desk accessories

  • Pip, a desk pet frog who yawns, scratches, gets startled, grumps, wanders and talks. Ask Pip a question, have it tell a joke, feed it or pet it.
  • Aquarium, a desktop fish tank, and Ant Farm, an ant colony simulation.
  • A dock for System 6 and 7, so the old Mac launches apps like a modern one.

modules.html:
Screensavers and demos

Native modules for Berkeley Systems' After Dark 2.0, the 90s screensaver everyone remembers, and a small demoscene set pushing the 68000: a cube, plasma, a starfield, a tunnel and the obligatory spinning donut.

Most projects include a floppy disk image you can mount in an emulator or copy to real hardware.
